speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you noticed the tremors in your hands, and do they occur when you are at rest or only when you are using your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a resting tremor starting in one hand and progressive memory loss is very concerning. Have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in his movements, and has he experienced any falls or changes in his gait?

The results of the neurological exam and the MRI will be crucial in distinguishing between Parkinson's disease with dementia and other neurodegenerative conditions like Lewy Body Dementia. Have you noticed any episodes where his vision blurs or doubles, or does he experience sudden fluctuations in his alertness throughout the day?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Alzheimer's Disease.

The combination of progressive amnestic symptoms (memory loss affecting daily tasks) with posterior cingulate/precuneus hypometabolism on PET scan, in the absence of synucleinopathy markers or significant midbrain atrophy, strongly supports Alzheimer's Disease.
